sample_unit: radiology questions (104 expert-curated plus 65 board-exam questions)
models_evaluated: 25 LLMs spanning general-purpose, reasoning-optimized, and clinically fine-tuned models (0.5B to 670B parameters)

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy with multi-step retrieval grounding versus zero-shot and conventional online RAG
links.effect: RaR improved mean diagnostic accuracy vs zero-shot (75% vs. 67%; P = 1.1e-7) and vs conventional online RAG (75% vs. 69%; P = 1.9e-6). Reduced hallucinations, with clinically relevant evidence in 46% of cases.
links.quote: RaR significantly improved mean diagnostic accuracy versus zero-shot prompting (75% vs. 67%; P = 1.1 × 10<sup>-7</sup>) and conventional online RAG (75% vs. 69%; P = 1.9 × 10<sup>-6</sup>).

unlisted_practices: Multi-step iterative retrieval and reasoning framework (question summarization, evidence retrieval, answer synthesis) to improve LLM accuracy
Selecting mid-sized deployable LLMs augmented with retrieval instead of very large models

screen.reason: Evaluates whether adding a multi-step retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounding safeguard improves diagnostic accuracy and reduces hallucinations across 25 LLMs on radiology question datasets.
